name: Prepositions at the end
subtitle: In questions, the preposition usually goes to the end: What are you waiting for? Who did you talk to? The same happens in clauses that describe a noun: the flat I live in.

concept.exampleHtml: What are you waiting for? — Who did you talk to? — This is the flat I live in.

qa.html: A verb + preposition (wait for, talk to) stays together in a question. The question word comes first, then the normal question order, and the preposition goes last: You are waiting for a parcel. → What are you waiting for? You talked to Priya. → Who did you talk to?

Use who for people and what for things. With a place, use where … from / to: Who are you going with? What are you looking at? Where does she come from? The preposition is the same in the answer: I'm waiting for the 9.15 train.

The same idea works in a clause that describes a noun. This is the flat. I live in it. → This is the flat I live in. You can add that or who, but you don't need to: the friend (who) I went with, the song (that) I was listening to. See Relative clauses.
Very formal writing can put the preposition first: To whom did you speak? The flat in which I live. This sounds stiff in normal speech. Ending a sentence with a preposition is correct English.

✗ What are you waiting? → ✓ What are you waiting for?
✗ Who did you talk yesterday? → ✓ Who did you talk to yesterday?
✗ This is the flat I live. → ✓ This is the flat I live in. (and not ✗ the flat I live in it)

concept.noteHtml: Which verb takes which preposition is in Verbs + prepositions: first learn wait for, then ask What are you waiting for?. The question word and the normal question order are in Wh- questions. The same word order in a reported question is on the page Indirect questions: I don't know who she is talking to. In short answers, keep the preposition with the noun or pronoun: Who did you talk to? — To Amira. or Amira.

rounds.label: 1 · Ask a question
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence. Ask about the object with What or Who. Put the preposition at the end.

example.prompt: She is waiting for a parcel.

items.prompt: He is talking to his manager.
They are looking at a map.
I'm going out with Kwame.
items.answer: Who are you going out with?

items.prompt: She is thinking about her holiday.
We listened to a podcast.
Priya comes from India.

rounds.label: 2 · Join the sentences
rounds.instruction: You hear two short sentences. Join them into one, as in the example. The preposition stays at the end.

example.prompt: This is the flat. I live in it.
example.answer: This is the flat I live in.

items.prompt: That is the man. I work for him.
items.answer: That is the man I work for.

items.prompt: Here is the book. I told you about it.
items.answer: Here is the book I told you about.

items.prompt: This is the song. I was listening to it.
items.answer: This is the song I was listening to.

items.prompt: She is the friend. I travelled with her.
items.answer: She is the friend I travelled with.

items.prompt: That is the girl. I am talking about her.
items.answer: That is the girl I am talking about.

items.prompt: This is the town. I come from it.
items.answer: This is the town I come from.

exercises.title: Who, what or where?
exercises.hint: Who is for people, what is for things, where is for places.

rows.term: He is looking at a map.
We are talking about the film.

exercises.title: Complete the question with the preposition.
exercises.hint: The sentence before the question shows which preposition you need.

items.prompt: Amira is waiting for a parcel. — What is she waiting ___?
items.why: She waits for a parcel, so the question ends in for.

items.prompt: I'm going to the cinema with Diego. — Who are you going ___?
items.why: You go with a person, so the question ends in with.

items.prompt: Zofia comes from Poland. — Where does she come ___?
items.why: She comes from a place, so the question ends in from.

items.prompt: Tom is looking at the sky. — What is he looking ___?
items.why: He uses his eyes on the sky: look at.

items.prompt: We talked about the film. — What did you talk ___?
items.why: The topic is the film: talk about.

items.prompt: It depends on the price. — What does it depend ___?
She is worried about her exam. — What is she worried ___?
items.why: The adjective goes with about: worried about.

items.prompt: I'm listening to the radio. — What are you listening ___?

exercises.hint: The preposition stays after the verb, at the end of the clause.

exercises.title: Question and answer: what goes together?
exercises.hint: Look at the question word and the preposition. They show what the answer is about.

exercises.title: Gap text: A message to a friend.
exercises.hint: Fill in the preposition that goes at the end.

segments.text:
Hi Diego,

Thanks for your message! You asked who I live
. I share a flat with two students from my course. It is the first flat I have ever lived
. Do you remember the film I told you
? We can watch it on Friday. Olga wants to know which city you moved
. The holiday I am saving money

is in July, so I am working a lot.

See you soon,
Zofia
